BIG-IP (LTM, AAM, AFM, Analytics, APM, ASM, DNS, FPS, GTM, Link Controller, PEM, WebSafe)

description: Attackers in a privileged network position may be able to obtain TCP sequence numbers (SEQ) from the BIG-IP system for a short period of time (up to 4 seconds) that will be reused in future connections with the same source and destination port and IP numbers.
impact:
Attackers in a privileged network position can spoof SEQ to be used by a future connection.

Note: This vulnerability is specific to BIG-IP virtual servers. However, some network scanners may incorrectly identify this issue as CVE-2002-1463. Additionally, this vulnerability only affects BIG-IP platforms equipped with the HSBe2 chip. For more information, refer to K14779: Overview of BIG-IP SYN cookie protection (11.3.x - 12.x).
mitigation: To mitigate this vulnerability, you can disable hardware SYN cookie processing by setting the connection.syncookies.algorithm database key to 'software.' For more information, refer to K16500: Overview of the connection.syncookies.algorithm database key.
recommended_actions:
If you are running a version listed in the Versions known to be vulnerable column, you can eliminate this vulnerability by upgrading to a version listed in the Versions known to be not vulnerable column. If the table lists only an older version than what you are currently running, or does not list a non-vulnerable version, then no upgrade candidate currently exists.

Only BIG-IP platforms equipped with the HSBe2 chip are vulnerable.
title: K68401558: BIG-IP virtual server TCP sequence numbers vulnerability
